mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing market (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by housing strength, resulting in flat to slightly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for two consecutive months, coupled with rising real savings (RSAFS), indicates supply-side weakness and excess liquidity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 for 2 consecutive months AND RSAFS > previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.0% while FEDFUNDS remains above 3.5% signals disinflation with restrictive policy, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by > 100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below -1% for five consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, is a leading indicator of weakening consumer demand and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month by > 1% for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1.0% and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a supply-side recovery coinciding with tight labor markets, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month by > 1.0% AND UNRATE < previous month by > 0.2pp and < 3.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.
